overallFinding.summary: Binance has an active AFSA-registered Kazakhstan entity and licence. The current licence explicitly lists permitted investment types Future and Option. Public Kazakhstan-facing surfaces remain separated from account-level eligibility; documented KZT rails are historical/current-status-unconfirmed unless a live provider surface is separately verified; named P2P method pages are surface-only; snippet-only product signals remain under review; referral terms are dynamic and do not prove Kazakhstan or CBW campaign eligibility.
overallFinding.recommendation: Treat Binance Kazakhstan as licensed and publicly reachable with claim-bound caveats. Do not publish current rail, universal product eligibility, named P2P method availability, snippet-only product status, or referral eligibility more strongly than the corrected evidence supports.

methodologyNotes: No login, registration submission, KYC submission, referral submission, deposit, withdrawal, trade, or account testing was performed.
Official-source-first hierarchy was applied by claim type rather than by a universal source-tier rule.
Search-snippet-only official records were retained but explicitly downgraded and caveated.

quickAnswerCandidates.answer: Binance is publicly reachable from Kazakhstan and AFSA-licensed BN KZ Technologies Limited currently holds active licence AFSA-A-LA-2024-0028. But technical reachability, legal authorization, registration success, and product-by-product eligibility are different questions and should not be collapsed into one yes/no answer.

Binance’s Kazakhstan entity, BN KZ Technologies Limited, appears in the AFSA public register with active licence AFSA-A-LA-2024-0028 dated 2024-09-25. The register shows a Digital Asset Trading Facility licence plus related regulated activities, but product scope still needs to be read carefully activity by activity.

Public sign-up and KYC flows are visible for both personal and entity accounts. Binance’s public guides show identity verification is required, and Kazakhstan KZT bank rails add local checks such as IIN-backed identity documents and, for Freedom Bank withdrawals, a matching IBAN.
Official Binance guides document Freedom Bank KZT deposit/withdrawal and Kazakhstan-issued Mastercard cash-out processes, but current live operational availability was not independently confirmed.
The KZT P2P marketplace and named payment-method pages are visible. Named method pages alone do not prove active offers, both directions or resident eligibility.

The current AFSA licence explicitly lists Future and Option, and public product surfaces exist. Account-level appropriateness, KYC/compliance and eligibility remain conditional; snippet-only product signals remain under review.

Binance still carries historical security and regulatory baggage, including the 2019 hack and the 2023 U.S. settlement. At the same time, Binance publicly states that user assets are backed 1:1 plus reserves and that SAFU remains its emergency fund, now denominated in USDC.
A public referral offer was visible at the checked date, but amounts and terms are dynamic. Kazakhstan eligibility and any CryptoBonusWorld campaign binding remain unconfirmed.
